correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the argument for the displayed map with literal first-coordinate linear multiplier −1. For x₀≠0, |x_n| decreases to a limit U. If U>0, |x_{n+1}/x_n|→1 forces y_n→0; the identity x_n=y_{n+1}−by_n then contradicts U>0. Once x_n→0, summation of the stable filter with |b|<1 gives y_n→0. The axis orbit x₀=0 is exactly (0,b^n y₀). For other orbits let q_n=x_n², r_n=y_n/x_n, s_n=1/q_n and D=1+b. The exact r-recurrence can be treated along the orbit as affine with slope −b(1+y_n²), eventually uniformly contractive, and constant term tending to −1. Thus r_n→−1/D, and Δs_n=2r_n²+r_n⁴q_n→c=2/D², giving q_n∼1/(cn). In the r equation the first forcing after subtracting its limit is −q_n/D³, and geometric convolution first gives r_n+1/D=O(1/n). Subtracting −q_n/D⁴ then leaves a stable recurrence forced at O(n⁻²), since q_{n+1}−q_n=O(q_n²). This proves the stable-fiber expansion. The increment has coefficient H=4/D⁵+1/D⁴=(5+b)/D⁵ on q_n, so s_n=cn+O(log n). Subtracting cn+(H/c)log n leaves increments O(log n/n²); their absolute summability and tail estimate give finite C and O(log n/n). Sign alternation and the ratio limit give both signed amplitudes, including the b-independent transverse one. Inspected the supplied symbolic/finite-iterate checker without executing it; a finite set of orbits cannot establish these quantifiers or the asymptotic error.
residual_risks: No uniformity near b=±1; the x₀=0 exception must not be included in the nonzero-tail formula. The result is for the map with a minus sign, regardless of external parameter conventions.

Generic critical exponent comparison in arXiv:2602.04091v1
value.rationale: For this previously studied map the result gives more than the usual local power law: it accounts for every finite initial state, isolates the stable-axis exception and shows that the first accumulated correction to inverse-square growth is logarithmic with a controlled remainder and a finite orbit-dependent offset. This distinguishes geometric transients and critical relaxation in an exact example and gives physical-coordinate coefficients against which local normal-form approximations can be checked.
residual_risks: The offset is not evaluated in closed form, and no drift bound uniform in b is supplied. The result has the scope of one natural critical map, not a general flip theorem.
